messages:
Maya: Heads-up — we had 3 interactive GPU sessions preempted in us-west2 during the 02:00-03:00 window. Latency-sensitive routes hit user-facing errors. Anyone tracking a pattern?
Ross: saw the alerts. Spot reclaim rate spiked for the older nvidia-a100 pool. Noticed many batch jobs draining into the same region.
Devin: @Maya can you paste the trace? are these dedicated or mixed-pool instances?
Maya: mixed-pool. root trace: `req id 0x7fa2` — model-serve process got SIGTERM, graceful shutdown timeout hit, restart failed fast = 503s to clients.
Caroline: that matches what we warned about with the current preemptible fallback: interactive tasks fall back to smaller GPU flavor but we didn't enable automatic warm-up in the hot pool.
Devin: Suggestion: create a tiny reserved hot-pool (1-2 GPUs per region) pinned for interactive low-latency routes and use spot for scale. On preempt, route to hot-pool or a degraded-mode CPU-only path.
Maya: agree. We need controlled failover rather than full restart. Can we implement an interrupt-hook that checkpoints model state and extends TTL?
Ross: we already have the hook framework in infra: `interrupt-hookd`. It can emit a graceful checkpoint event + annotate job with `preempted_at`. We just need to wire the traffic router to honor annotated jobs for fast warm standby.
Caroline: operational plan: (1) reserve 2x `hot-pool` GPUs in us-west2, (2) change routing policy `prefer-hot-then-spot` for latency routes, (3) modify scheduler to prefer preempt-protected nodes for jobs flagged `interactive=true`.
Devin: batch jobs: move heavy retrain to off-peak windows and into the cheaper asia-south1 spot regions. We should also add queue priority weights: interactive=100, batch=10, background=1.
Maya: can we implement auto-shift of batch to off-peak via schedule rules? e.g., `if local_hour in [0,6] then prefer(region=asia-south1, cost<0.4)`
Ross: yep. We can add a policy DSL rule and simulator. I'll add a test to the capacity planner to estimate cost delta.
Caroline: interruption handling checklist: `SIGTERM` -> `interrupt-hookd` triggers checkpoint, save KV-state to s3, send webhook to conv-svc, switch traffic to hot-pool, schedule retry with exponential backoff. We should document time budgets: checkpoint 30s, backfill warm 60s.
Devin: quick config snippet I propose for scheduler (pseudo):
```
policy {
  route: latency_sensitive -> [hot-pool (capacity 2), spot-pool (capacity 50)]
  on_preempt: checkpoint && route_to(hot-pool) || degrade_to(cpu-fallback)
  batch_windows: { start: 00:00, end: 06:00, preferred_regions: [asia-south1] }
}
```
Ross: Also add a `cooldown` on the spot eviction loop to avoid oscillation: if a node is reclaimed, add 10m hold before migrating new interactive tasks into that specific physical host group.
Maya: sounds good. What about cost impact of reserving hot-pool? need quick numbers.
Dev in: I ran a back-of-envelope: reserving 2 A100s in us-west2 bumps baseline infra cost ~+8% but reduces 503s and the customer impact cost >> savings on CTAs. I'll put numbers in the capacity planner PR.
Caroline: action items: Ross -> add policy DSL + simulator (ETA: EOD), Devin -> PR for interrupt-hookd integration (ETA: tomorrow), Maya -> write runbook for hot-pool failover steps and update runbook link in alerts, Ops-bot -> add auto-page rule on >2 preemptive errors in 30m.
ops-bot: Alert rule created: `preemptive-interactive-errors-us-west2` -> pages on severity >=2 within 30m. docs: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/spot-fallback (draft).
Maya: thanks team. Once Ross posts the simulator results we'll schedule a weekend rollout to minimize customer impact.
Ross: I'll also add a canary flag so we can flip `prefer-hot-then-spot` only for 5% of traffic first.
Devin: one more note — we should tag spot instances with `spot_score` metric and evict lower-score batch tasks first. That reduced disruptions in the EU last month.
Caroline: agreed. Closing loop: update the SLO playbook with new time budgets and rollback plan.
Maya: closing — will follow up with PR links and the rollout schedule. Thanks :thumbsup:
